He began '''weaving''' coconut fronds when he was a young child after seeing traditional weavers selling their pāpales (a traditional style of crownless hat) and baskets to tourists on the beach.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[spin]] a [[cocoon]] or a [[web]]. #: {{ux|en|Spiders '''weave''' beautiful but deadly webs.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[unite]] by close [[connection]] or [[intermixture]]. For he on honey-dew hath fed,
And drank the milk of Paradise.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|of an animal}} To move the head back and forth in a [[stereotyped]] pattern, typically as a symptom of stress. =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|to move by turning and twisting|dodge}} * Albanian: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * Japanese: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|заворачивать|impf}} * Slovene: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to make (a path or way) by winding in and out or from side to side}} * Bulgarian: * French: * Māori: * Portuguese: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} ====References==== * {{R:Century}} * {{R:Webster 1913}} {{cln|en|strong verbs|irregular verbs}} {{C|en|Hair|Weaving}}

==English== {{chemical element box|en}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=metal|:inh|enm:led}} From {{inh|en|enm|led}}, {{m|enm|leed}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lēad|t=lead}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laud|t=lead}}, possibly borrowed from {{der|en|cel-pro|*ɸloudom}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*plewd-|t=to flow}}. More at {{m|en|flow}}. * {{sense|graphite in a pencil}} Graphite was once believed to be a form of lead; see {{m|en|black lead}} and {{m|en|plumbago}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alt|mul|♄||alchemy}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/lɛd/|a=RP,GA,CA]}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-lead.wav|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-lead-metal.oga|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Tesco250-lead.wav|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/led/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{rhyme|en|ɛd|s=1}} * {{hmp|en|led}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} [[file:Lead electrolytic and 1cm3 cube.jpg|thumb|Electrolytically refined pure lead]] # {{senseid|en|Q708}} {{lb|en|uncountable}} A heavy, [[pliable]], [[inelastic]] metal [[element]], having a bright, bluish color, but easily [[tarnish]]ed; both [[malleable]] and [[ductile]], though with little [[tenacity]]. It is easily [[fusible]], forms [[alloy]]s with other metals, and is an ingredient of [[solder]] and [[type metal]]. [[atomic number|Atomic number]] 82. #: {{syn|en|mul:Pb|plumbum}} # {{senseid|en|Q1382947}} {{lb|en|countable|nautical}} A [[plummet]] or mass of lead attached to a line, used in [[sound]]ing [[depth]] at sea or to estimate [[velocity]] in [[knots]]. # A thin [[strip]] of [[type metal]], used to [[separate]] lines of type in printing. # {{lb|en|uncountable|typography}} Vertical space in advance of a row or between rows of text. Also known as ''[[leading]]''. #: {{ux|en|This copy has too much '''lead'''; I prefer less space between the lines.}} # [[sheets|Sheet]]s or [[plate]]s of lead [[used]] as a [[covering]] for [[roofs]]. # {{lb|en|countable}} A [[roof]] covered with lead [[sheet]]s or [[terne]] [[plate]]s. #* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Building|passage=I would have the tower two stories, and goodly '''lead'''s upon the top.}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis|passage=These rooms were on a level with the apartments of our friends Bows and Costigan next door at No. 4; and by reaching over the communicating '''leads''', Grady could command the mignonette-box which bloomed in Bows’s window.|43}} # {{senseid|en|Q1936519}} {{lb|en|countable}} A thin [[cylinder]] of [[graphite]] used in [[pencil]]s. #: {{syn|en|pencil lead}} # {{lb|en|slang}} [[bullet|Bullets]]; [[ammunition]]. #: {{ux|en|They [[pump|pumped]] him full of '''lead'''.}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=2012|genre=[[hip-hop]]|artist={{w|Kendrick Lamar|Kendrick Lamar}}|title={{w|Backseat Freestyle|Backseat Freestyle}}|passage=All my life I want money and power

Related to {{cog|ang|līþan|t=to go, travel}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|lede|leed||both|_|obsolete}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/ˈliːd/|[ˈlɪi̯d]}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-lead-guide.oga|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|iːd|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|lead}} * {{hmp|en|leed|lede|lied|t3=song}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|led}} # {{senseid|en|guide}}{{lb|en|heading|transitive}} ''To [[guide#Verb|guide]] or [[conduct#Verb|conduct]].'' ## To [[guide]] or [[conduct]] with the hand, or by means of some physical contact connection. ##: {{ux|en|a father '''leads''' a child}} ##: {{ux|en|a jockey '''leads''' a horse with a halter}} ##: {{ux|en|a dog '''leads''' a blind man}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Matthew|15|14|passage=If a blind man '''lead''' a blind man, both fall down in the ditch.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|4|29|passage=They thrust him out of the city, and '''led''' him unto the brow of the hill.}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Poems|poem=L'Allegro|passage=In thy right hand '''lead''' with thee / The mountain nymph, sweet Liberty.}} ##* {{RQ:Asbjornsen Braekstad Tales|page=271|passage=As he was going home to the palace, he met an old woman '''leading''' a golden goose.}} ## To [[guide]] or conduct in a certain [[course]], or to a certain place or end, by making the way known; to show the way, especially by going with or going in advance of; to [[guide]] somebody somewhere or to [[bring]] somebody somewhere by means of [[instruction]]s. ##: {{ux|en|The guide was able to '''lead''' the tourists through the jungle safely.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Exodus|13|21|passage=The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to '''lead''' them the way.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Psalms|23|2|passage=He '''leadeth''' me beside the still waters.}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Poems 1673|sonnet=XXI|passage=This thought might '''lead''' me through the world’s vain mask. Content, though blind, had I no better guide.}} ##* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=I|passage=I stumbled along through the young pines and huckleberry bushes. Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path that, I cal'lated, might '''lead''' to the road I was hunting for. It twisted and turned, and, the first thing I knew, made a sudden bend around a bunch of bayberry scrub and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn.}} ## {{lb|en|figuratively}}: To [[direct]]; to [[counsel]]; to [[instruct]]. ##: {{ux|en|A good teacher should '''lead''' their students to the right answer.}} ## To conduct or [[direct]] with [[authority]]; to have direction or charge of; to [[command]], especially a [[military]] or [[business]] unit. ##: {{syn|en|spearhead}} ##: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' a political party}} ##: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' the search team}} ##* {{RQ:South Sermons|chapter=A Sermon Preached Before the University at Christ-Church, Oxon|year=1664|passage=Christ took not upon him flesh and blood that he might conquer and rule nations, '''lead''' armies, or possess places.}} ## To draw or direct by [[influence]], whether good or bad; to prevail on; to [[induce]]; to entice; to allure. ##: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' someone to a righteous cause}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|Matthew|6|13|passage=And '''lead''' us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil|footer=From the [[Lord's Prayer]]. Modernized spelling.}} ##* {{RQ:King James Version|2 Timothy|3|6|passage=Silly women, laden with sins, '''led''' away by divers lusts.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1649|author=King {{w|Charles I of England}}|title=w:Eikon Basilike|passage=He was driven by the necessities of the times, more than '''led''' by his own disposition, to any rigor of actions.}} ## To influence towards a belief, a conclusion, etc. ##: {{ux|en|The evidence '''leads''' me to believe he is guilty.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To guide or conduct, as by accompanying, going before, showing, influencing, [[directing]] with authority, etc.; to have [[precedence]] or preeminence; to be first or [[chief]]; — used in most of the senses of the transitive verb. # {{lb|en|heading}} ''To begin, to be ahead.'' ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To go or to be [[in advance]] of; to [[precede]]; hence, to be foremost or chief among. ##: {{syn|en|head|front}} ##: {{ux|en|the big sloop '''led''' the fleet of yachts;  the Guards '''led''' the attack;  Demosthenes '''leads''' the orators of all ages}} ##* '''1600''', {{w|Edward Fairfax}}, The ''{{w|Jerusalem Delivered}}'' of {{w|Torquato Tasso|Tasso}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1819|author=w:Leigh Hunt|title=Abou Ben Adhem |passage=And lo! Ben Adhem's name '''led''' all the rest.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|passage=“Well,” I answered, at first with uncertainty, then with inspiration, “he would do splendidly to '''lead''' your cotillon, if you think of having one.” ¶ “So you do not dance, Mr. Crocker?” ¶ I was somewhat set back by her perspicuity.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[proceed]] [[in front of]] others; to go first. ##: {{ux|en|The standard-bearers '''led''' and the rest of the marchers followed.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be more advanced in [[technology]] or [[business]] than others. ##: {{ux|en|It '''leads''' in the information technology sector.}} ## {{lb|en|heading|sport}} ### {{lb|en|transitive|cards|dominoes}} To [[begin]] a game, round, or trick, with ###: {{ux|en|to '''lead''' trumps}} ###: {{ux|en|He '''led''' the ace of spades.}} ### {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be [[ahead]] of others, e.g., in a [[race]]. ### {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have the highest interim [[score]] in a [[game]]. ### {{lb|en|baseball}} To step off [[base]] and move towards the next base. ###: {{ux|en|The batter always '''leads''' off base.}} ### {{lb|en|shooting}} To aim in front of a moving [[target]], in order that the [[shot]] may hit the target as it passes. ### {{lb|en|transitive|climbing}} To [[lead climb]]. {{rfclarify|en|"to lead climb" is intransitive(?)}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To tend or reach in a certain spatial [[direction]], or to a certain place. #: {{ux|en|the path '''leads''' to the mill}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Two Gentlemen of Verona|act=V|scene=ii|passage=The mountain-foot that '''leads''' towards Mantua.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be a cause of. {{+obj|en|:to}} #: {{syn|en|lead to}} #: {{ux|en|gambling '''leads''' to other vices}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-28|author=w:Joris Luyendijk|volume=189|issue=3|page=21|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control Our banks are out of control]|passage=Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic […].  Until 2008 there was denial over what finance had become. ===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=suitable|:inh|enm:fit<t:an adversary of equal power><unc>|tree=1}}
Possibly from {{inh|en|enm|fit||an adversary of equal power}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} further origin. ===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leyp-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|leven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lǣfan|t=to leave}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laibijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*laibijaną|t=to let stay, leave}}, causative of {{m|gem-pro|*lībaną|t=to stay, remain}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyp-|t=to stick; fat}}.

Cognate with {{cog|ofs|lēva|t=to leave}}, dialectal {{cog|nl|loven|t=to have left over, save, keep}}, {{cog|osx|lēvian}}, {{cog|goh|leiban|t=to leave}}, {{cog|non|leifa|t=to leave over}} (whence {{cog|is|leifa|t=to leave food uneaten}}, {{cog|sv|leva|t=to leave}}), {{m|is|lifna|t=to be left}} (whence {{cog|da|levne}}). More at [[lave#Etymology_2|lave]], [[belive#Etymology_1|belive]].

The noun is attested since the 19th century, with earliest references to billiards.

{{en-verb|~s|leaving|left}}

# To have a consequence or remnant.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause or allow (something) to [[remain]] as [[available]]; to [[refrain]] from taking (something) away; to [[stop short]] of consuming or otherwise depleting (something) entirely.
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' my car at home and took a bus to work.}}
##: {{ux|en|The ants did not '''leave''' so much as a crumb of bread.}}
##: {{ux|en|There's not much food '''left'''. We'd better go to the shops.}}
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=7|passage={{...}} St. Bede's at this period of its history was perhaps the poorest and most miserable parish in the East End of London. Close-packed, crushed by the buttressed height of the railway viaduct, rendered airless by huge walls of factories, it at once banished lively interest from a stranger's mind and '''left''' only a dull oppression of the spirit.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/david-van-tassel David Van Tassel]; [http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/lee-dehaan Lee DeHaan]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/wild-plants-to-the-rescue Wild Plants to the Rescue]
|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=Plant breeding is always a numbers game.{{nb...}}. The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation,{{nb...}}. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better. These rarities may be new mutations, or they can be existing ones that are neutral—or are even selected against—in a wild population. A good example is mutations that disrupt seed dispersal, '''leaving''' the seeds on the heads long after they are ripe.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive|copulative}} To cause, to result in.
##: {{ux|en|The lightning '''left''' her dazzled for several minutes.}}
##: {{ux|en|Infantile paralysis '''left''' him lame for the rest of his life.}}
##: {{ux|en|She '''left''' disappointed.}}
##: {{ux|en|The accident '''left''' the car a heap of twisted metal.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1899|author=w:Stephen Crane
|title=s:Twelve O'Clock|chapter=1
|passage=There was some laughter, and Roddle was '''left''' free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up{{nb...}}.”}}
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=23|passage=The slightest effort made the patient cough. He would stand leaning on a stick and holding a hand to his side, and when the paroxysm had passed it '''left''' him shaking.}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408| issue=8845| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/http://www.economist.com/news/asia/21582043-villagers-enjoy-sunlight-after-dark-out-gloom Out of the gloom]| passage=[Rural solar plant] schemes are of little help to industry or other heavy users of electricity. ## {{senseid|en|deposit (something) and withdraw oneself}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To put; to place; to deposit; to deliver, with a sense of withdrawing oneself.
##: {{ux|en|'''Leave''' your hat in the hall.}}
##: {{ux|en|We should '''leave''' the legal matters to lawyers.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' my sewing and went to the window to watch the falling snow.}}
##* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|5|24|passage='''Leave''' there thy gift before the altar and go thy way.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|IV|iii|passage=The foot / That '''leaves''' the print of blood where'er it walks.}}
# To depart; to separate from.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[let be]] or do without interference.
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' him to his reflections.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''leave''' my hearers to judge.}}
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''leave''' it to you to decide.}}
## {{senseid|en|depart or depart from}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[depart]] from; to end one's connection or [[affiliation]] with.
##: {{ux|en|His bow and arrow never '''leave'''s him.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' the country and I '''left''' my wife.}}

## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[end]] one's [[membership]] in (a group); to terminate one's affiliation with (an organization); to [[stop]] participating in (a project).
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' the band.}}
## {{lb|en|euphemistic|transitive}} To [[die]] (the object denotes those affected by the death).
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To depart; to [[go away]] from a certain place or state.
##: {{syn|en|egress|q1=U.S., formal|absent|exit|make tracks|set forth|Thesaurus:leave}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:der|enm:connexioun|tree=+}}
From {{inh|en|enm|conneccioun}}, {{m|enm|connexioun}}, {{m|enm|conneccyon}}, {{m|enm|conneccion}}, from {{der|en|la|connexionem}} (nominative {{m|la|connexio||a [[conclusion]], [[binding]] [[together]]}}), from {{m|la|connectō}}, an alternative spelling of {{m|la|cōnectō||to [[bind]] [[together]]}}, from compound of {{m|la|co-||[[together]]}} and {{m|la|nectō||to [[bind]]}}.

In [[American English]] mid-18c., spelling shifted from {{m|en|connexion}} to ''connection'' (equivalent to {{suffix|en|connect|ion}}), thus making {{m|en|connexion}} British dated and ''connection'' in international use.
